resources.string: Choose the app network (may traverse the device VPN) or the configured 127.0.0.1 HTTP proxy. Proxy mode sends HTTP CONNECT to the specified IP/host:port and NEVER retries directly. CONNECT 200 proves only proxy tunnel acceptance. Verified TLS requires a system-trusted certificate matching the selected SNI. Neither proves device-wide VPN or DNS-leak safety.
Targets (IP, hostname, IPv4 CIDR or inclusive range)
Validate TLS certificate and SNI hostname
Explicit SNI (required for IP TLS; blank uses hostname for domain targets)
Scan %1$d targets with at most %2$d sockets, %3$d ms timeout per target, in %4$s mode? These app-network requests may traverse an active VPN. No VPN profile or tunnel state will be changed.
Invalid targets, port, timeout, SNI or pass count. Use 1–3 passes, up to 128 unique IPv4/IPv6/hostname targets; oversized ranges are rejected. Literal IP TLS needs an explicit DNS SNI.
Cannot verify the current default-network session. No sockets were opened. This diagnostic needs Android 7 or later with an available default network.
Route: app network; may traverse a device VPN. Not a proxy or DNS leak test.
Network changed during the scan; it was stopped. Measurements are historical, not current-route proof.
Scan stopped. Unfinished targets are unknown, not failures.
The report contains target IPs, hostnames, SNI values, proxy/app route, individual pass results, and timestamps. The selected app will receive these details. Share anyway?
Use configured local HTTP CONNECT proxy; never direct fallback
Configured local HTTP proxy port or listener unavailable. Probe stopped without direct fallback.
Route: configured local HTTP CONNECT proxy on 127.0.0.1. CONNECT 200 alone is not verified TLS.
Probe %1$d targets × %2$d passes = %3$d attempts; at most %4$d concurrent sockets; %5$d ms timeout each. Mode: %6$s. Route: %7$s. No automatic direct fallback, profile import or VPN switch. Continue?
Verified repeatable proxy TLS: %1$d of %2$d observed candidate groups (requires at least 2 complete passes).
